translations.name: Squat -> Stand Coordination

translations.description:
Lie on your back with your knees bent, or sit comfortably. Breathe in slowly into your belly and let your pelvic floor relax and gently lengthen downwards, without pushing or straining. Breathe out and let the pelvic floor return to its resting position. Repeat slowly for several breaths.

The reverse Kegel trains relaxing the pelvic floor, the opposite of the contraction in a regular Kegel exercise.
translations.name: Gentle Reverse Kegels

translations.description:
Lie on your back and pull your knees towards your armpits. Hold the outside of your feet, your ankles or your shins, with the soles of your feet facing the ceiling and your shins roughly vertical.

Gently pull your feet down to open the hips while keeping your lower back and head on the floor. Hold the position and breathe calmly, you can also rock gently from side to side.
translations.name: Happy Baby

translations.description:
Stand upright with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging at your sides and feet hip-width apart. For a larger range of motion, stand with the balls of your feet on a step or a weight plate.

Rise up onto your toes as high as you can and pause briefly at the top. Then lower your heels slowly until you feel a stretch in your calves. Keep your knees straight but not locked and your upper body upright.
translations.name: Dumbbell Calf Raise

translations.description: Use the same technic as your normal squat. Except that you make a pause at the bottom of the squat for about 1-2 seconds, in other words a bit longer than your normal squat.
translations.name: Paused Squats
notes: same technic as your normal squat
same speed as your normal squat
pause for 1-2 seconds at the bottom

translations.description:
Go into a one-legged kneeling position and grab the cable from the lowest position.

Rotate the upper torso to get into the starting position and bend the upper torso a little bit sidewise.

Place the unused hand on the knee.

Pull the cable while rotating the upper torso.
translations.name: Single-Arm Cable Row with Rotation (Floor)

translations.description: A gentle stretch to restore full knee extension. Sit with one leg stretched out in front of you and the heel propped on the floor or a low surface, so the knee is unsupported. Place both hands on the thigh just above the kneecap. Keeping the leg relaxed, gently press down through the hands toward the floor until you feel a stretch behind the knee, and hold for about three seconds before releasing. The pressure should produce a stretch, never sharp pain. Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions, then switch legs.
translations.name: Seated Knee Extension with Overpressure
notes: Hold about three seconds, then release fully before the next rep.
Often prescribed after knee surgery or injury to restore full extension.
Keep the heel propped and the leg relaxed; the hands do the work.
Press gently toward a stretch, never into sharp pain.

translations.description: A banded walking drill for the glutes and hip stabilisers. Place a mini band around both thighs just above the knees, or around the ankles for a harder version. Stand with feet hip-width apart so the band is under tension, then sink into a quarter-squat with the chest up. Walk forward with small diagonal steps, pushing each leg out against the band and keeping the knees tracking over the toes rather than letting them fall inward. Walk forward for the prescribed number of steps, then walk backward to return, keeping the band under tension throughout.
translations.name: Banded Monster Walk
notes: Step out and forward on a diagonal rather than straight ahead.
Take small, controlled steps instead of long ones.
Keep tension on the band the whole time; don't let the knees collapse inward.
Stay in a quarter-squat with the chest up.

translations.description: Stand on a step or a sturdy raised surface with the balls of both feet on the edge and the heels hanging off, holding a rail or wall for balance. Let one or both heels drop below the level of the step until you feel a stretch through the calf, and hold. Keep the knee straight to stretch the gastrocnemius, or bend the knee slightly to bias the soleus lower down. Hold for the prescribed time, typically 30 seconds, without bouncing, then switch sides if stretching one leg at a time.
translations.name: Step Calf Stretch
notes: Bend the knee slightly to shift the stretch to the soleus.
Lower slowly and hold steady rather than bouncing.
Hold a rail or wall for balance.
Keep the stretching leg straight to bias the gastrocnemius.

translations.description: A balance and proprioception drill. Stand on one leg with the knee slightly bent and the other foot lifted clear of the floor, then close your eyes and hold the position. Without visual feedback the ankle and hip stabilisers have to do the work, so expect noticeable wobble. Stand within reach of a wall, counter or chair so you can steady yourself if needed. Hold for the prescribed time, then switch legs. Commonly prescribed in rehabilitation after ankle or knee injury.
translations.name: Single-Leg Balance with Eyes Closed
notes: Keep the standing knee soft, not locked.
Let the foot and ankle work; small wobbles are the point.
Stand near a wall or counter so you can catch yourself.
Closing the eyes removes visual input, which is what makes this hard.

aliases: Kettlebell Body Circle on One Leg
translations.description: A balance drill that adds a moving load. Stand on one leg with the knee slightly bent, holding a kettlebell in one hand. Pass the kettlebell around your body in a circle, handing it from one hand to the other in front and behind you, while keeping your balance on the standing leg. Keep the hips level and the torso upright; the shifting weight of the bell constantly changes your centre of mass, which is what trains the hip and ankle stabilisers. Complete the prescribed number of circles, reverse direction, then switch legs. Use a light bell to start.
translations.name: Single-Leg Balance with Kettlebell Circles
notes: Move the bell smoothly, passing hand to hand behind the back.
Change direction halfway through the set.
Start light; the weight is a balance challenge, not a strength one.
Keep the hips level and square as the bell travels.

translations.description:
How to Perform It

  • Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral or overhand grip.
  • Hinge at the hips, pushing your glutes back, until your torso is roughly 45–75 degrees to the floor. Keep a slight bend in your knees.
  • Let the dumbbells hang directly below your shoulders with arms fully extended.
  • Keep your back flat, chest up, and core braced — avoid rounding your spine.
  • Pull the dumbbells up toward your ribcage/hips, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top.
  • Pause briefly at the top of the movement.
  • Lower the dumbbells back down under control to the starting position.
  • Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Key Coaching Cues

  • Hinge from the hips, not the lower back
  • Keep the spine neutral throughout — no rounding
  • Lead with the elbows, not the hands
  • Avoid using momentum or jerking the weight up
  • Control the eccentric (lowering) phase rather than letting the weights drop
translations.name: Bent Over Dumbbell Rows (Two Arms)

translations.name: Alternate Walking

Full-body mobility and dynamic warm-up routine (3–5 minutes) to prepare joints, muscles, and the cardiovascular system for workout.

Movement Flow:

Deep Breathing & Arm Raises: Inhale while raising arms laterally overhead, exhale as you lower them.

Knee Bends: Soft, rhythmic knee flexions synchronized with arm swings.

Arm Circles: Large full-range arm rotations forward, then backward to open up the chest and shoulder girdle.

Chest Expansion: Cross arms in front of the chest and open wide to the sides.

Side Bends: Reach overhead to stretch the lateral torso left and right with a smooth side flexion.

Forward & Back Bends: Gently hinge at the hips to reach forward, then return upright with a mild spinal extension.

Torso Twists: Swing arms side-to-side to rotate the spine and loosen the core.

Ankle Mobility / Light Bounces: Soft heel lifts or light bouncing on toes to warm up lower leg joints and tendons.
translations.name: Radio Taiso
notes: Keep movements smooth, controlled, and continuous. Do not force any range of motion.

translations.description:
Kelso shrugs are a variation of scapular shrugs designed primarily to train scapular retraction, with particular emphasis on the middle trapezius, rhomboids, and, secondarily, the lower trapezius. Unlike conventional shrugs, the goal is not to elevate the shoulders toward the ears, but rather to pull the shoulder blades backward.

They are typically performed with the chest supported on an incline bench, using either dumbbells or a barbell:

  1. Lie face down on an incline bench, with your arms extended toward the floor.
  2. Keep your elbows almost completely locked throughout the movement.
  3. Starting with the shoulder blades slightly protracted, retract them, trying to bring them closer together.
  4. Keep your chest firmly supported on the bench; avoid turning the movement into a row by extending your torso.
  5. Briefly hold the fully retracted position, then return in a controlled manner, allowing the shoulder blades to separate.
translations.name: Kelso Shrugs

translations.description:
1. Starting position: Lie flat on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor (or stand/sit upright).
  2. Exhalation: Fully exhale all the air from your lungs through your mouth.
  3. Contraction: Draw your navel in towards your spine as far as possible, pulling your stomach inward and up under your ribcage.
  4. Hold: Hold this isometric contraction without breathing for 10 to 20 seconds.
  5. Release: Slowly inhale through your nose to release the tension and relax your abdominals.
  6. Repeat: Rest briefly and perform the desired number of sets.
translations.name: Stomach Vacuum
notes: Fully empty your lungs before drawing your stomach in.
Focus on expanding your chest slightly during the hold while keeping the stomach sucked in.
Keep your lower back flat against the floor when performing the lying variation.
Do not force or arch your back during the movement.

translations.description:
Starting position

Step into the captain's chair (vertical knee raise station). Rest your forearms on the pads and hold the handles. Keep your upper body upright, look straight ahead and press your back against the pad, without rounding or arching it. Your legs are almost straight with a slight bend in the knees, your feet are off the floor and your legs are together.

Movement

Pull your bent legs up, bringing your knees towards your chest. Only go as high as you can while keeping good form, with your legs together the whole time. Then lower your legs again while inhaling, without putting your feet back on the floor.
translations.name: Captain's Chair Knee Raise

translations.description:
Starting position

Step into the captain's chair (dip station). Rest your forearms on the pads and grip the handles firmly. Keep your back upright and close to the pad and look straight ahead. Bend your legs so that your thighs and shins form roughly a right angle.

Movement

Raise your knees while turning your legs slightly to one side, about 30-45 degrees, keeping your thighs parallel to the floor. Then do the same to the other side. You can pause briefly in the middle or go straight to the other side.
translations.name: Captain's Chair Oblique Knee Raise

translations.description: Weighted neck flexion is an isolation exercise designed to strengthen the anterior (front) neck flexor muscles by bringing your chin toward your chest against external resistance (most commonly a light weight plate, resistance band, or neck harness).
translations.name: Weighted neck flexion
notes: 1. Lie flat on your back on a weight bench with your neck and head hanging off the edge. Keep your shoulders firmly planted on the bench.
2. Hold a light weight plate (5–10 lbs to start) against your forehead using your hands solely to hold the plate in place, not to push or pull it.
3. Slowly lower your head back toward the floor in a controlled motion until you feel a mild stretch in the front of your neck. Avoid hyper-extending the spine.
4. Tuck your chin inward first, then curl your head upward until your chin approaches your chest. Pause for a second at top contraction before lowering under control.

translations.description: Strength training exercise where you push a weight away from your body using one leg at a time on a leg press machine. It helps to improve leg strength, balance, and muscular symmetry by isolating each leg individually. This exercise is particularly useful for identifying and correcting muscle imbalances between your legs.
translations.name: Single leg press

translations.description: Perform a row using gymnastic rings, but with the body position somewhere between vertical and horizontal. Go closer to horizontal to make it harder.
translations.name: Incline Row - Rings
notes: Don't let your shoulders shrug up
Rings/bar to chest and shoulder blades fully retracted (pinched together) at the top

translations.description:
Starting Position

• Feet: Place the soles of your feet flat against a vertical wall, with your toes or balls of your feet on the floor. • Hands: Position your hands on the floor shoulder-width apart, directly under your lower chest or solar plexus. • Body: Keep your core tight, glutes squeezed, and head in a neutral position. Your knees should hover a few inches above the floor without touching it.

Movement Pattern

  1. Lower Down: Flex your elbows (tucked around 45 degrees) to lower your chest toward the floor, stopping just a few centimeters short of touching the ground.
  2. Rock Back: As you press upward through your arms, push your hips backward and bend your knees, rocking your weight toward your heels while keeping your shins nearly parallel to the floor.
  3. Drive Forward: Explode forward from your lower-body/crouched position, shifting your weight back into the starting push-up plank stance to complete the repetition.

Key Tips for Proper Form

• Keep Knees Low: Do not let your knees or hips pike high up in the air; keep the motion low and horizontal. • Maintain Wall Contact: Keep the soles of your feet pressed against the wall so you don't lose your leverage. • Engage the Core: Avoid arching your lower back by tilting your pelvis backward and bracing your abs.
translations.name: Tyson push-ups

translations.description: Start on all fours with your palms flat on the floor. Slowly rock forward and backward, keeping your hands planted. Move only within a comfortable, pain-free wrist range to gently improve mobility and flexibility.
translations.name: Wrist rocks

translations.description: Start in a straight-arm plank with your hands under your shoulders. Keep your elbows locked and move only your shoulder blades: let your chest sink slightly, then push the floor away to spread the shoulder blades. Move in a comfortable, controlled range.
translations.name: Scapular Pushups

translations.description: Dumbbell squats with elevated heel position. Stand on either squat wedges or weight plates to raise heels higher than toes, while holding the dumbbells on your sides.
translations.name: Dumbbell cyclist squat

translations.description:
Push ups for targeting triceps.

  • Start with a plank position with your hands directly below your shoulders, feet together.
  • When descending, keep your elbows pinned to your sides. Upper arms straight back.
  • Lower until your chest touches the floor, then return.
translations.name: Triceps push up

translations.description: Extend your right arm straight across your chest toward the left. Hook your left arm around your right elbow and pull your right arm a little closer to your body. Keep your shoulder down as you do this. Repeat on the other side.
translations.name: Cross-Body Stretch

translations.description: Extend your right arm straight out in front of you, with your palm facing up (fingers pointing toward the floor). Using your left hand, gently pull the fingers of your right hand toward you until you feel a stretch in your forearm and biceps.
translations.name: Wrist Stretch

translations.description: Stand on one leg (hold onto a wall if necessary). Use your hand to grasp the ankle of your other leg and gently pull your heel toward your buttocks. Make sure your knees stay close together and that you push your pelvis slightly forward (avoid arching your back).
translations.name: Quadriceps Stretch

translations.description: One of the best exercises for the rectus abdominis muscles. Lie on your back with your legs straight and your arms close to your sides. Lift your head off the floor and raise your legs and arms about 15 centimeters off the floor. Your palms should face down, and look up at the ceiling. Now bend your legs and at the same time sit up so that your knees and chest almost touch. Only your buttocks are still on the floor. Your arms are now extended at shoulder height. Then slowly return to the starting position with your arms and legs extended and your head raised.
translations.name: V-Up

translations.description: A static hold from a pull-up bar with straight elbows and actively depressed, stabilized shoulders. Grip a secure bar and let your body hang under control. Keep your elbows straight and gently draw your shoulders down, away from your ears. Maintain this active shoulder position without pulling up, swinging, or repeatedly moving the shoulder blades. Hold for up to 30 seconds. Stop earlier if your grip opens, shoulder control deteriorates, or pain occurs. Record actual seconds, grip, and any assistance used. This is distinct from a relaxed passive dead hang or a moving scapular pull-up.
translations.name: Active Hang
notes: Keep elbows straight and shoulders actively stabilized. Stop for grip loss, loss of shoulder control, or pain.

translations.description: A static bodyweight support with both hands and feet on the floor and hips raised in a pike position. Place your hands and feet securely on the floor, then raise your hips. Keep your elbows straight and actively push the floor away through your shoulders. Maintain a controlled, stationary position without bending your elbows, lowering your head for push-up repetitions, or raising your feet onto a surface. Hold for up to 30 seconds. Stop earlier for loss of alignment, loss of active shoulder support, or pain. Record actual seconds, hand and foot spacing, and alignment. This is the floor variation, not a pike push-up or an elevated-feet pike hold.
translations.name: Pike Hold (Floor)
notes: Keep both hands and feet on the floor, elbows straight, and shoulders actively pushing. Stop for loss of alignment or pain.
